n: The Lord speaks to the elders in Kirtland in September 1831, shortly before Joseph moved to Hiram. Some had returned from Missouri with hard feelings toward one another.
He wants them to overcome the world, and so he will show them compassion.

f.w: overcome the world

n: Some among them have sinned, but this once, for his glory and their salvation, he has forgiven them.
He will be merciful because he has given them the kingdom.
The keys of the kingdom’s mysteries will remain with Joseph Smith while he lives, as long as he obeys.

f.w: the keys of the mysteries of the kingdom

n: Some have looked for reasons to accuse Joseph without cause.

f.w: sought occasion against him
f.g: Looked for an excuse to criticize or accuse him.

n: Joseph has sinned too, but the Lord forgives all who confess and seek forgiveness, unless they have sinned “unto death.” Prophets are not perfect.

f.w: sinned unto death

n: The Lord’s disciples of old held grudges against one another and suffered for it.

f.w: sorely chastened

n: Therefore forgive one another. Whoever refuses to forgive carries “the greater sin.” Unforgiveness hurts the one who withholds it.

f.w: ye ought to forgive one another

n: One of the best-known verses on forgiveness: the Lord will forgive whom he will, but we are required to forgive everyone.

f.w: of you it is required to forgive all men

n: Instead of holding grudges, say in your heart: let God judge between us and repay according to deeds. Leaving judgment to God frees the heart.

f.w: let God judge between me and thee

n: Unrepentant sinners who won’t confess should still be brought before the Church as scripture directs.

f.w: bring before the church

n: This is done not from lack of compassion but to glorify God and honor his law. Forgiveness and accountability work together.
This is the reason they are to do these things.
The Lord was angry with Ezra Booth and Isaac Morley for not keeping the law. Booth had since left the Church.

f.w: him who was my servant Ezra Booth
f.g: “Who was” signals Booth had apostatized; he wrote critical letters published in an Ohio newspaper.

n: They looked for faults and condemned what wasn’t evil, so the Spirit withdrew. Yet Isaac Morley has been forgiven.
Edward Partridge has also sinned, and Satan seeks his soul—but if he and others repent when shown their error, they will be forgiven.
Sidney Gilbert should return to his agency in Zion after a few weeks.
He should share what he has seen and heard, so the disciples don’t perish.
Isaac Morley’s farm was ordered sold so he wouldn’t be tempted beyond his strength or give harmful counsel.

f.w: tempted above that which he is able to bear

n: Frederick G. Williams should not sell his farm, because the Lord wants a strong foothold in Kirtland for five years to save some. The Church did remain strong in Kirtland until 1838.

f.w: Frederick G. Williams
f.g: A physician who later served as a counselor in the First Presidency.

n: After that, no one will be held guilty for going to Zion with an open heart. The Lord requires people’s hearts.

f.w: I, the Lord, require the hearts of the children of men

n: “Today” lasts until Christ comes. It is a day of sacrifice and tithing; those who are tithed will not be burned at his coming. In 1831 “tithing” referred broadly to offerings; the specific law came in 1838.

f.w: it is called today
he that is tithed shall not be burned

n: After “today” comes the burning: the proud and wicked will be like stubble. No one remaining in Babylon will be spared.

f.w: stubble
f.g: Dry stalks left after harvest—quick to burn.

f.w: Babylon

n: If they believe him, they will work while it is still today.

f.w: labor while it is called today

n: Newel K. Whitney and Sidney Gilbert should not sell their store yet, until the remaining Church members in Kirtland move to Zion.
The Lord’s law forbids going into debt to enemies.

f.w: to get in debt to thine enemies
f.g: Being indebted to hostile people gives them power over you.

n: But the Lord himself may take and pay as he sees fit.
As agents, they are on the Lord’s errand; whatever they do by his will is his business.

f.w: on the Lord's errand
f.g: Doing the Lord’s work as his representatives.

n: He has set them to provide for the Saints so they can obtain an inheritance in Zion.
The Lord’s words are sure: they will obtain it.
But everything must happen in its time.

f.w: in their time

n: A beloved verse: don’t grow weary in doing good, for you are laying the foundation of a great work. Great things grow from small ones.

f.w: be not weary in well-doing
out of small things proceedeth that which is great

n: The Lord requires the heart and a willing mind. The willing and obedient will enjoy the good of Zion.

f.w: the willing and obedient shall eat the good of the land

n: The rebellious will be removed from Zion and will not inherit it.
The rebellious are not truly of Ephraim’s blood—the covenant lineage entrusted with the gathering.

f.w: the blood of Ephraim
f.g: Ephraim, son of Joseph, whose descendants carry special responsibility in the latter-day gathering.

n: The Church is like a judge sitting on a hill, an elevated place, to judge the nations.

f.w: a judge sitting on a hill

n: Zion’s inhabitants will judge matters pertaining to Zion.
Liars and hypocrites will be exposed, and false apostles and prophets made known.

f.w: they who are not apostles and prophets

n: Even the bishop and his counselors will be condemned and replaced if unfaithful. No calling exempts anyone.

f.w: the bishop, who is a judge

n: Zion will flourish, and the Lord’s glory will rest on her.

f.w: the glory of the Lord shall be upon her

n: She will be an ensign—a banner—to the world, and people from every nation will come.

f.w: an ensign
f.g: A flag or banner to rally around.

n: Nations will tremble because of her and fear her “terrible ones”—those made awe-inspiring by God’s power.

f.w: her terrible ones
